items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And it’s like Ben Riley the drummer. He used to tell me, “If you stop playing fast, call me, I’d like to work with you.”

ctx.x: Exactly, yeah. And it’s easier playing like that. And after a while I enjoyed playing, maybe a little faster than that. And I enjoy that because it says more. You know you have to think and construct a nice melodic solo. And I love playing ballads now more than I used to. In fact I’m now playing the melody, maybe phrasing it differently, which is almost the same concept as a conductor with classical music. He’s not going to change the notes but he may add his own conception of phrasing for a particular work. And…
I always feel sorry for the bass players too. It just seems like such — after a while the locked —
